To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a carboryl‐selective NMR probe that is able to detect and quantify free keto and aldehydes in complex mixtures, and that we have used this probe to analyze the metabolite profile of a cancer cell line.

we have designed an NMR‐selective probe for carbonyl‐functionalized metabolites, which can be easily incorporated in a variety of cell culture and tissue samples, and which allows the selective detection of carbonyl compounds, including ketoses and aldoses, in complex mixtures of metabolite extracts.
the aminooxyl‐N‐15 reagent is a carbonyl-selective probe that can be used to detect and discriminate keto- and aldehydes in complex mixtures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel 15N‐detected 1H NMR methods to selectively detect and identify metabolites that contain free carbonyl groups.
the development of new analytical methods for the detection and identification of metabolites.
the development and application of a new NMR‐based method to detect and discriminate carbonyl‐bearing compounds in complex biological mixtures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 15N aminooxy‐based approach is a very powerful tool for the detection and discrimination of a large number of carbonyl metabolites in complex mixtures.
the 15N editing approach is a valuable addition to the NMR toolbox, and it will be of particular interest for those researchers who are not familiar with NMR.

1H‐15N‐detected NMR spectroscopy of metabolites is a very powerful tool to detect carbonyl‐functionalized compounds in complex mixtures, and the aminooxygenation approach is a very useful method to select and discriminate between different carbonyl‐bearing metabolites in a mixture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carbonyl‐specific aminooxy‐probe provides a new and highly sensitive tool for detection and discrimination of ketoses, aldoses, and aldehydes in complex mixtures.
we have developed a new tool for the detection and discrimination of a large number of metabolites that are not readily detectable by 1H NMR.
15N‐detected 1H‐NMR spectroscopy can be used for the chemoselective detection of carbonyl compounds and for discrimination between ketones and aldehyde functions in complex biological mixtures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
15N‐detected NMR can be utilized to selectively identify and quantify carbonyl‐bearing compounds in metabolite extracts, even when the carbonyl function is masked by a hydroxyl group.
the 15N editing technique can be combined with the aminooxygenation reaction to selectively and chemically detect free keto and aldehydes in a complex metabolite mixture.
the 15N editing of NMR data is a very powerful tool for selective detection of carbonyl compounds in complex mixtures.
